raw_case_text:
A 21-year-old Caucasian man was admitted to the University Hospital of Patras, Western Greece, with fatigue, fever up to 39 C, and retrosternal pain. He denied anorexia, night sweats, and generalized malaise. No significant past medical history was reported. There were no risk factors for HIV infection, no recent travel outside Greece, and no exposure to animals. The patient denied smoking and drinking, and also no allergies were noted.
On physical examination, the temperature was 39.0 C, the heart rate was 90 bpm with sinus rhythm, and the blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg. The patient was respiratory stable (respiratory rate 16/min and oxygen saturation 98% on room air). No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy was identified. There were no murmurs, rubs, or gallops, and the lungs were clear on auscultation and percussion. The abdomen was nondistended, with normal active bowel sounds and mildly tender in the midepigastrium but without rebound or guarding. No liver or spleen enlargement was noted. No abnormalities like clubbing, cyanosis, or edema were found on all extremities. The rest of the examination was unremarkable.
Electocardiography (ECG) revealed a sinus rhythm with ST elevation (ST 2 mm in I, II, aVL, and V4-V6) (Figure 1). Furthermore, laboratory tests showed a low platelet count 134.000 (normal range 150.000-400.000 Kappa/mul), raised aspartate aminotransferase (193 U/L, upper normal limit (UNL) 40 U/L) and alaninoaminotranferase (42 U/L 40 U/L), high CPK levels (2166 mg/dl, upper normal limit 190 mg/dl) with CPK-MuBeta lower than 10% of total CPK (112 mg/dl), troponine (TaunI) 48.51 ng/ml, and CRP 4.60 mg/dl. The hemogram was normal (Table 1). Chest X-ray image did not reveal any abnormalities. Blood and urine cultures were taken on admission. The transthoracic echocardiography Doppler showed wall motion abnormalities and absence of pericardial effusion. Accordingly, a cardiac MRI using delayed enhancement was performed (Figures 2 and 3) revealing recent myocardial damage with edema and fibrosis in the middle and upper left and right lower wall and increased left ventricular dimensions with normal systolic function.  In addition, cardiac MRI revealed overriding of the right ventricle with normal systolic function
Serology for Influenza A and B, parvovirus B19, EBV, and CMV, ECHO virus, Coxsackie virus, HSV, VSV, and adenovirus, Coxiella burnetii, Chlamydia, Leptospira spp., and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were negative. On day 3 of hospitalization, Brucella melitensis was isolated from two consecutive blood cultures. The Brucella serum agglutination test (SAT) was positive >1/1280, so a diagnosis of Brucella-related myocarditis was made. Treatment with oral rifampicin (900 mg once daily) and doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) along with intravenous gentamycin (320 mg once daily) was immediately commenced. Gentamycin was administered for ten days. The patient recalled that he had consumed unpasteurized goat cheese a month ago. After five days of treatment, the patient was clinically improved, asymptomatic, and fever was regressed. No signs of cardiac arrythmias or other ECG abnormalities on serial ECGs, during hospitalization, were noted. On discharge day, all laboratory tests were normal (Table 2). Patient had a total antibiotic course with Doxycycline and rifampicin for 6 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 21-year-old male presented with acute retrosternal chest pain, fever up to 39 °C, and fatigue.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with acute retrosternal chest pain, high fever reaching 39 °C, and fatigue. He denied anorexia, night sweats, or generalized malaise.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant past medical history. Denied alcohol use, tobacco smoking, or high-risk behaviors for HIV. No recent travel outside Greece; denied animal contact. Epidemiological exposure: recalled consuming unpasteurized goat cheese one month prior to admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Retrosternal chest pain, fever, fatigue. Denied anorexia, night sweats, or generalized malaise. Home medications: none. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 39.0 °C, heart rate: 90 beats/min (sinus rhythm), blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg, respiratory rate: 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation: 98% on room air. Cardiovascular: no cardiac murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Respiratory: clear to auscultation and percussion. Abdomen: soft, mildly tender in the midepigastrium without rebound or guarding; no hepatosplenomegaly. Extremities: no clubbing, cyanosis, or peripheral edema. Lymph nodes: no cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Platelet count 134,000/microL, AST 193 U/L, ALT 42 U/L, total CPK 2,166 mg/dL, CPK-MB 112 mg/dL, cardiac troponin I 48.51 ng/mL, CRP 4.60 mg/dL. Hemogram normal (Table 1). Electrocardiogram (ECG): sinus rhythm with 2 mm ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, aVL, and V4-V6. Chest X-ray: normal. Transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE): left ventricular wall motion abnormalities without pericardial effusion. Infectious serologies negative: Influenza A and B, Parvovirus B19, EBV, CMV, Echovirus, Coxsackievirus, HSV, VZV, Adenovirus, Coxiella burnetii, Chlamydia, Leptospira spp., and Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
objective.advanced_workup: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (delayed enhancement): recent myocardial damage with myocardial edema and fibrosis in the middle and upper left and right lower ventricular wall, increased left ventricular dimensions with normal systolic function, and overriding of the right ventricle with preserved systolic function.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute Brucella-induced myocarditis. Confirmed by 2 consecutive blood cultures isolating Brucella melitensis on day 3 of hospitalization and Brucella serum agglutination test (SAT) positive at >1/1280. Viral and atypical causes of myocarditis (Coxsackie, Influenza, Parvovirus B19, EBV, CMV, ECHO, Coxiella burnetii, Leptospira, Mycoplasma) were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Initiated on triple therapy with IV gentamicin (320 mg once daily for 10 days), oral rifampicin (900 mg once daily), and oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily). Within 5 days, fever regressed, symptoms resolved, and repeat serial ECGs showed no arrhythmias. Discharged with normalized cardiac biomarkers and liver enzymes to complete a 6-month course of oral doxycycline and rifampicin.
